reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling (NVA4) in northern Virginia publishes 11 MW of IT load capacity, representing roughly 275 racks or approximately 2,200 accelerators at typical AI training density. This is a modest single-facility footprint, below the scale where infrastructure becomes a binding constraint on large-scale model training.

Sterling ranks 22nd among the 25 Virginia facilities with published capacity figures, holding 0.7% of the state's total. Virginia lists 330 mapped data center locations but only 25 disclose power specifications, indicating most of the state's infrastructure capacity remains undisclosed. Within the published set, Sterling is a mid-tier facility by power consumption.

The 128,715 square feet of technical space and absence of listed certifications are consistent with a regional colocation facility serving enterprise and cloud tenants rather than a hyperscale AI training campus. Sterling's individual contribution to AI compute scaling is minor compared to the largest regional operators, and the facility's undisclosed expansion plans leave unclear whether its role in the regional compute ecosystem will grow.
